title: A size read off a screenshot is the size the type really was
goal: Redlining a screenshot is what this app is mainly for, and reading a label back into text is now the fastest way to get a number off one. On one of the study captures those numbers come back about nine per cent high: row labels that are 13 points on screen say 28 px where 26 is the true answer. Somebody writing a spec off the Size menu writes the wrong number, and has no way to know. Measure how far off the reading really is against type of a known size, say why, and close the gap or say in the app how close the number is.
notes:
NOT REPRODUCED BY THE MANAGER, filed p2 as something to look into rather than p1. The screen has been locked since 2026-09-15 so no walk can run, and the loop owns the build directory, so this was read in the code and taken from a runner´s own measurement rather than measured again here.

Where it comes from: the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-17-label-size.json, first item. Its words: the size is still about 9 per cent bigger than the type really was; those row labels are 13 points on screen and come back as a 28 point layer on a 2x capture, where 26 would be the true answer. That audit deliberately did not file it, saying it needs its own study rather than a near-twin task. This is that study.

Evidence that cuts the other way, and the first thing to check: Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/ReadPageWeightFixtureTests.swift says the Effects panel rows fit at 22.2, 21.4, 22.4, 22.4 and 21.9 points on a 2x capture. If those rows are 11 points on screen that is dead on, which would mean the error is not a constant nine per cent and is specific to that capture or that face. Settle which before changing anything.

The mechanism: Sources/PhotonzRender/TextReader.swift, best(_:in:against:inkHeight:scale:) around line 690 and size(of:in:matchingInkHeight:scale:). It sets the string at a probe size, measures the ink height of that render, and scales so the two ink heights match, then nudges over sizeFactors and keeps the best overlap. That is exact only if ink in a capture is measured the same way as ink in a fresh render; antialiasing and the coverage threshold in inkBounds() are the obvious place for a few per cent to come from.

A size a redline is written from is the reason this sits under measure-redline rather than under the reading feature it landed in.

--- WHAT THE STUDY FOUND (2026-09-17, runner) ---

Measured, not read. Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/ReadSizeGroundTruthTests.swift sets type at a size it chooses, photographs it, and reads it back.

1. The MEASUREMENT is sound. Read at the scale the type was photographed at (layerScale == captureScale), the reading lands within 1.2% of the truth across 18 combinations of size, weight, family and scale. The real settings-pane-2x rows read 13.00 at layerScale 2; the real effects-panel-2x rows read 10.00. Whole numbers, from a measurement that rounds to nothing.

2. The GAP is the conversion into document points. A Retina capture opens as a document measured in its own pixels (Document.withBaseImage sets canvasSize = ref.pixelSize), so layerScale is 1 while captureScale is 2. The size is then re-fitted at layerScale, and THAT number is what the Size menu shows: 28.38 where 26 is the truth on the settings pane, 22.22 where 20 is the truth on the effects panel. +6.5% on type this study set itself, +9.2% and +11% on the two real fixtures.

3. The CAUSE is the system font optical size, and nothing else. "Launch at login" set at 13pt drawn at 2x is 182x25 pixels of ink; set at 26pt drawn at 1x it is 168x24. Same em, same pixels, 7.7% apart. Helvetica Neue and SF Mono, which carry no opsz axis, are pixel-for-pixel identical both ways. So it is NOT antialiasing, NOT the 0.1 coverage floor in inkBounds(), NOT rounding and NOT the sizeFactors search. The task notes guessed those; they are ruled out and the ruling-out is a test (theSystemFontIsADifferentDrawingAtLabelSizeAndAtHeadingSize).

4. The note here guessed the Effects panel rows were 11pt and "dead on". They are 10pt and read 22. So the error is NOT specific to one capture or one face; it is constant and systematic. That question is settled.

5. Consequence, and why this is a decision rather than a patch: a 13pt label photographed at 2x cannot be reproduced by ANY point size. 28.4 covers the same pixels, 26 is the size the type was. queue/decisions/2026-09-17-read-size-two-answers.png shows both against the original ink.

FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE ANSWER: the true size is already computed and thrown away. TextReader.measure() scores every face at captureScale (Measured.scores), which IS the accurate number; settle() then re-fits at layerScale and returns that instead. Whichever option wins, the true size is scores-at-captureScale multiplied by captureScale/layerScale. Note also that the panel says px everywhere and DocumentUnit.strays() fails anything saying pt, so any new readout is in px.
acceptance: A ground-truth round trip exists as a test: set a string at a known point size at a known capture scale, read it back, compare. Several sizes, several faces, both 1x and 2x.
The test says how far off the reading is at each of those sizes, and that number is written into the audit as a table.
The cause is named in plain words: why a freshly set string and the same string in a capture do not measure the same ink.
Where the gap can be closed it is closed, and the round trip lands within a point of the type that made it.
Where it genuinely cannot be closed, the app says so rather than claiming a number it cannot support, and the audit says which of the two happened.
The two fixture captures that already have numbers behind them still read the way ReadPageWeightFixtureTests pins them, or that test is updated with the reason in its comment.

Try it: Photonz Dev, release Next, next-read-every-label is on by default. Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png, pick the Background row, run Separate into Layers, press Read the Words, then pick the six row labels from Launch at login down to Copy to clipboard and read the Size menu in the Text section.

log.note: Reproduced with ground truth, and the cause is named. Set 13 point SF Pro, photograph it at 2x, read it back: at the scale it was set the reading is right (worst of 18 combinations 1.2%). Read into a document measured in the capture's own pixels - which is every Retina screenshot this app opens - the same labels come back +6.5% (28.4 where 26 is the truth), identically for every label. Cause: the system font carries an optical size. 'Launch at login' set at 13 and drawn at 2x is 181x25 pixels of ink; set at 26 and drawn at 1x it is 168x24. Same em, same pixels, 7.7% apart. Helvetica Neue and SF Mono, which have no optical axis, come out identical both ways. So it is not antialiasing, not the 0.1 coverage floor, not rounding, and not the search.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Shipped the study and blocked on the fix. Done and verified: acceptance 1 (ground truth round trip, 3 faces x 2 scales x 3 sizes plus a whole-page pass at 1x and 2x), 2 (the table is in the audit and printed by the test), 3 (cause named: the system font's optical size, with the alternatives ruled out by a test), 6 (ReadPageWeightFixtureTests and ReadRunAsTextFixtureTests, 41 tests, all green, nothing in production changed). Not done: 4 and 5, because closing the gap means choosing between two numbers that cannot both be right, which is the card now on the dashboard. Left rough, none of it earning its own task: the error is 6.5 to 11 per cent depending on the words rather than one constant, so no single correction closes it; the true size is already computed at capture scale inside TextReader.measure and thrown away when settle refits at layer scale, which is the hook whichever option wins; the panel says px everywhere and DocumentUnit.strays fails anything saying pt, so any new readout is in px. Searched the queue three ways (size read off a screenshot, optical size, Size menu) and nothing else covers any of it. Ran label-size-walk for the audit pictures: it passed all 60 steps and took 6 real captures under a locked screen; claimed --none since it is not this task's to fix.

The study is done, committed and audited (queue/audits/2026-09-17-read-size-truth.json). The size is 6.5 to 11 per cent high on a Retina capture, every label by the same amount, and the cause is the system font's optical size: a 13 point label photographed at 2x cannot be reproduced by any point size. Closing it means picking which number the Size menu says, which is on the dashboard as a card with a picture of both against the original ink.

decision "A label read off a Retina screenshot: should the Size menu say the size the type really was, or the size that makes the retyped words cover the picture exactly?" resolved: Say the size the type really was
